steps.prompt: Can you hold “friendship” in your hand? What about a friend? What’s the difference?

cards.title: Concrete nouns
cards.body: A concrete noun names something you can see, hear, touch, taste or smell: a drum, thunder, pizza, a pebble. If one of your five senses can notice it, it’s concrete.

cards.title: Abstract nouns
cards.body: An abstract noun names an idea, feeling or quality you can’t touch: courage, fear, freedom, friendship, honesty. Many end in -ness, -dom, -hood or -ship: kindness, freedom, childhood, friendship.

cards.title: Collective nouns
cards.body: A collective noun is one word for a group: a team of players, a flock of birds, a crowd of fans, a class of students. When the group acts as one, treat it as singular: “The team is ready.”

cards.title: Make big ideas real
cards.telling: She had a lot of courage.
cards.showing: Her courage showed in her steady hands as she lit the stage lights.
cards.note: Abstract nouns are powerful in essays (justice, safety, freedom), but readers understand them best when you connect them to something concrete.

prompts: Which abstract noun did you use, and what concrete detail helped show it?
Think of a topic you might write an essay about. Which abstract noun is at the heart of it?
